finding_records.evidence: Family and Type are absent from the normalized source header. Revision is also absent; this is received evidence, not a historical Revision 0.
finding_records.proposal: Family=Foundation; Type=Architecture; no invented Component or Class requirement. Introduce Revision=1 only when UPDATE produces the first working successor. Retain Document ID DF-FND-004 and Language English.
finding_records.closure_criterion: Header conforms to the adopted four-value Type rule; the input edition remains traceable; no normalization fields are imposed on the eight functional files.

finding_records.evidence: §1.7 presents four conceptual layers; §8.2 presents five, adding Preservation. Baselines appears under Governance in §§1.7.3/4.3 and under Preservation in §8.7, without a primary-allocation/participation distinction. ARC-004 §§4–11 lists seven structural areas.
finding_records.proposal: Explicitly name the five-concern conceptual view (Knowledge, Documentation, Governance, Discovery, Preservation), make §1.7 consistent or label its subset, and separately explain the seven-area structural organization. Foundation/Architecture are support areas; Knowledge/Preservation are conceptual views, not new structural directories. Baselines remains primarily allocated to Governance while contributing to Preservation.
finding_records.closure_criterion: All affected prose, summaries and diagrams label their view; one primary allocation per component; no new Knowledge or Preservation structural Layer is created by a conceptual view. ARC-004 count correction remains assigned to its own cycle.

finding_records.evidence: §3.12 describes META-DCL-001 using META=Family and DCL=Type as a current semantic structure, conflicting with permanent identity and mutable classification. §3.5 groups Title with identification without distinguishing a mutable label from the unique identity key.
finding_records.proposal: Qualify META-DCL-001 as a historical convention. Describe the adopted corpus representation DF-SSS-NNN: stable registered allocation series and number, independent of current Family/Type. Explain the unique Domain+Identifier identity and mutable Title. Identity preservation does not legitimize erroneous declarations; authorized corrections use a path-scoped map.
finding_records.closure_criterion: No current identity construction/validation depends on mutable classification; history is explicitly qualified; DF-FND-004 retains its ID; no global CLS-001 alias is introduced. Detailed representation ownership remains with Document Identity.

finding_records.evidence: §9.5 states: “All structural information should exist only once. Metadata constitutes the official source of that information.” This gives Metadata unqualified authority over structural/domain semantics. The chapter describes properties but does not connect element definitions, Schema, Profile and document-specific values.
finding_records.proposal: Narrow the authority: domain owners define identity, classification and lifecycle semantics; Metadata provides descriptors and their representation. At Blueprint level, summarize Dictionary definition, Schema organization, Profile usage restrictions and Instance values, retaining exactly one effective Profile per Instance. Do not fill the missing catalog or create Metadata Element IDs.
finding_records.closure_criterion: Each responsibility is assigned to an explicit owner; §9.5 and summaries no longer make Metadata the owner of every domain definition; the overview agrees with the adopted descriptor/schema/profile/instance distinction. MTD-003 Schema-defines-elements discrepancies and the incomplete catalog remain open until their own cycles.
finding_records.impact: Semantic authority and Metadata abstraction model

finding_records.evidence: §8.11 labels Metadata→Registry→Knowledge Graph→Baselines as dependencies and claims unidirectionality, while §3.16 states Registry and other components consume Metadata. The same unlabeled arrow notation also denotes navigation, lifecycle and information flow elsewhere.
finding_records.proposal: Label every relationship diagram by purpose. For mandatory dependencies use consumer→provider, with a typed table stating source, target, contract and justification. Registry→Metadata expresses descriptive consumption. Treat chronological/navigation flows separately; assess Knowledge Graph and Baselines contracts rather than infer adjacent mandatory dependencies. Do not hide a mandatory cycle by renaming its edges.
finding_records.closure_criterion: Dependency direction agrees with consumption statements; conceptual refinement, overview reference, lifecycle and navigation are distinct relationship kinds. No mandatory DAG or inter-layer consistency is declared until affected ARC/MTD contracts are reconciled.

finding_records.evidence: §9.10 states “Relationships are represented only in the Knowledge Graph”, while §5.6 places Relationships in Registry Entry and ARC-005 §7.2 assigns relationship management to Relationships. Registry Entry repeats Status/Version beside Metadata, leaving authoritative versus derived values ambiguous.
finding_records.proposal: Relationships owns relationship definitions/records; Knowledge Graph provides their semantic network view; Registry indexes existence/discovery and may expose referenced or derived views. Distinguish one logical document catalog entry from edition records. Mark indexed Metadata values as derived from identified source editions; single semantic authority does not forbid traceable projections.
finding_records.closure_criterion: No competing owners for relationship semantics; Registry/Knowledge Graph representations have explicit provenance and synchronization rules at contract level. Registry does not redefine Identity or Classification. Legitimate projections are not called semantic duplication.
finding_records.impact: Registry, relationship and graph responsibility boundaries

finding_records.evidence: Baselines is a snapshot/reference configuration (§§6.4/6.9), but the Included Documents diagram (§6.7) does not explicitly select immutable document editions. §8.10 ends every change flow with Baseline, potentially implying automatic new inclusion.
finding_records.proposal: A Baseline member references a document identity plus its exact Version/Revision or an equivalent immutable edition reference; physical evidence may carry a hash. Creating/editing a Draft does not alter an existing Baseline or confer membership. Make approval and explicit Baseline selection gates visible. Current/introduction/retirement Baseline in Registry is contextual membership information, not a universal single document state.
finding_records.closure_criterion: A prior approved edition can remain in an immutable Baseline while a new working edition is Draft and unassigned; later edits do not retarget the snapshot; no Baseline or approval record is fabricated. The Blueprint defines the conceptual contract, not a storage schema.
finding_records.impact: Edition selection, approval and snapshot semantics

finding_records.evidence: §4.10 distinguishes Version/Revision/Status, but §6.8 lists Document/Revision/Baseline as levels and omits Version. One active state per document (§4.5) versus two versions in the same state (§4.6) lacks an edition/current-view distinction.
finding_records.proposal: Use Document as the entity, Version/Revision as edition coordinates, Status as the state of the applicable edition and Baseline as a collective snapshot. Distinguish current working state from preserved historical edition states. Explain that checks do not imply approval. Reference the working review numbering convention rather than invent a framework-wide numbering history.
finding_records.closure_criterion: Version/Revision/Status/Baseline retain distinct meanings across all affected paragraphs and diagrams; future working corrections do not rewrite the received Approved/Baseline 1.0 evidence. No historical Revision 0 is invented for this source.

finding_records.evidence: “They are components of a documentation system” (§1.5.1), Documents under component headings and META Documents as normative documentation (§2.7) mix document entities, documentary roles and registered architectural capability components. Classification and Reviews are not explicit in the main Blueprint component responsibility overview, although ARC-005 assigns them capabilities.
finding_records.proposal: Distinguish entity, capability component and documentary role. Add Classification ownership and Reviews quality-assurance responsibilities to the conceptual overview; identify selective examples as selective. Recast META Documents as a historical/documentary designation, not a new current Family/Type/component or automatic normative-authority grant. State that functional files are maintained without normalized-header/ID requirements.
finding_records.closure_criterion: Document entities are not mistaken for new capability components; classification/quality assurance owners are visible; no Type Base/Core/META is created; the eight functional-file exclusions remain explicit. Detailed component enumeration stays owned by Architecture.
finding_records.impact: Concept/component distinction, classification and normalization scope

finding_records.evidence: The source states the components are stable, the architecture Mature and every listed area Consolidated. The received header is Approved, but the corpus does not provide complete implementation or release evidence, and current review findings remain unresolved.
finding_records.proposal: Preserve those statements as dated received architectural assessments, or qualify their scope as intended conceptual capabilities. Distinguish design documentation, implementation evidence, review conformity and formal approval. Do not silently revoke a historical approval declaration.
finding_records.closure_criterion: The working edition does not present this review as proof of maturity, full conformance or operational implementation. Historical assessments remain traceable.

finding_records.evidence: Integration contracts and the Blueprint’s “primary architectural reference” role have no explicit Related Documents/authority map to the responsible ARC/MTD/DID sources. FND-001 §13 states DF documents DMS/CMS functionality rather than implementing it; the Blueprint also uses operational management language.
finding_records.proposal: Add a scoped authority/reference table using existing identities and paths; distinguish DF conceptual contracts from external implementations/process execution. Include DMS as an external consumer/example consistent with FND-001 §13, without prescribing a new mandatory system hierarchy or deleting Governance/Automation concepts.
finding_records.closure_criterion: All newly added references resolve to the intended current source paths; responsibility boundaries are explicit and implementation independence is preserved. No unseen external DMS/CMS specification is claimed as reviewed.
finding_records.impact: Reference coverage and external execution boundary
